mainTopic: The קיטע's wooden leg: the end of the משנה, settling who permits and who forbids it on שבת, and whether it can become טמא מדרס.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a קיטע (amputee) and then begins the גמרא. The משנה gives רבי יוסי's view forbidding the wooden leg (קב) on שבת. It then rules on the טומאה of the קב, the knee supports, a crippled person's chair, and לוקטמין, and on whether each may be worn out on שבת or into the עזרה. The גמרא opens with רבא asking רב נחמן which name goes with which opinion in the קיטע dispute, and רב נחמן does not know. שמואל and רב הונא read the משנה as 'אין הקיטע', and רב יוסף adopts their reading. רבא בר שירא then shows from a scene in רב's study hall that רב reversed it: רבי מאיר permits and רבי יוסי forbids. The memory aid 'סמך סמך' fixes this, and the גמרא proves that שמואל and רב הונא later accepted רב's reading. Along the way, a plasterers' sandal is shown to be טמא מדרס because the plasterer walks home in it. Finally אביי and רבא argue whether a קב with a padding hollow can become טמא מדרס. Each brings a proof, and רבא's answer to אביי's walking-stick proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי forbids going out with the wooden leg
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר and forbids a קיטע to go out on שבת with his wooden leg.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of a dispute. רבי מאיר allowed the קיטע to go out with his wooden leg on שבת, and רבי יוסי says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole question is whether the wooden leg counts like clothing or a shoe, which may be worn out on שבת, or like a separate object, which would be carrying. רבי מאיר treats it like a shoe. רבי יוסי does not, so walking out with it would be carrying into רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbids, prohibits
An amputee, someone missing a leg (the subject of this משנה)
The wooden leg or stump that the amputee uses

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי's words 'אוסר' have no object written in them. They refer back to רבי מאיר's ruling about the wooden leg, which comes on the previous amud. רבי יוסי is not forbidding anything new.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei forbids it.
phrases.notes: Forbids going out on Shabbat with the wooden leg, which רבי מאיר permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the dispute that רבי מאיר opened on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, a קיטע may not go out on שבת with his wooden leg.

steps.title: A wooden leg with a padding hollow can become impure
steps.stepSummary: If the wooden leg has a hollow for padding, it counts as a container and can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it has a hollow for holding pads, it is susceptible to impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the שבת question to a טומאה question about the same wooden leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain wooden object usually cannot become טמא unless it has a בית קיבול, a space that holds things. If the wooden leg has a hollow on top where soft pads are placed to cushion the stump, that hollow is a receptacle. That gives it the status of a כלי עץ, so it can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A receptacle, a space that holds something
Soft pads or rags used for cushioning
Here it means susceptible to ritual impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule found all over the laws of טומאה: a wooden item without a receptacle generally cannot receive טומאה, and adding a receptacle changes that.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית קִיבּוּל כְּתִיתִין
phrases.english: And if it has a receptacle for pads
phrases.notes: A hollow at the top of the wooden leg where cushioning is placed.

phrases.english: it is susceptible to impurity.
phrases.notes: It now counts as a wooden vessel with a receptacle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית קִיבּוּל כְּתִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the same wooden leg but switches from the laws of שבת to the laws of טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wooden leg with a padding hollow can become טמא.

steps.title: Knee supports: impure through treading, allowed on שבת and in the Temple courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The קיטע's knee supports can become טמא through מדרס, may be worn out on שבת, and may be worn into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His supports can become impure through treading. One may go out with them on שבת, and one may enter the Temple courtyard with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a second item: the leather supports that a person missing both feet straps onto his knees so he can walk on them. It gives three rulings about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the supports are made to be walked on, a זב who wears them makes them an אב הטומאה through מדרס. They count like shoes for שבת, so wearing them out is allowed. For the עזרה, where shoes are forbidden, they do not count as real shoes, so they are allowed there.

keyTerms.meaning: Supports, coverings worn on the knees by someone who walks on his knees
Impurity passed on when a זב treads, sits, or leans on an item made for that use
The Temple courtyard, where shoes may not be worn

steps.confusionAlert: The same supports count as shoes for שבת but do not count as shoes for the עזרה. These are two separate laws, and each one has its own test of what counts as a shoe.

phrases.english: His supports are susceptible to treading-impurity,
phrases.notes: They are made to bear weight while walking.

phrases.english: and one may go out with them on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: They count as worn, like shoes, so wearing them is not carrying.

phrases.english: and one may enter the Temple courtyard with them.
phrases.notes: They are not considered real shoes for the courtyard ban.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wooden leg to a new item, the knee supports, and covers them under all three laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knee supports can become טמא through מדרס, are allowed outside on שבת, and are allowed in the עזרה.

steps.title: A cripple's chair and supports: impure through treading, forbidden on שבת and in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A crippled person's chair and hand supports can become טמא through מדרס. They may not be worn out on שבת and may not be brought into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His chair and his supports can become impure through treading. One may not go out with them on שבת, and one may not enter the Temple courtyard with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a contrast case. This is a person who cannot walk at all, sits on a small chair tied to him, and pushes himself along with supports on his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both this case and the knee-support case share the rule of מדרס, since the chair and supports are used for sitting and moving. They differ on the other two laws. The chair setup is not treated like something worn, as a shoe is, so taking it out on שבת counts as carrying. It is also not allowed into the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A chair, here a small seat attached to the crippled person
One may not go out (with it on שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: The three items get three different sets of rulings. The wooden leg is disputed for שבת, and it can become טמא only if it has a hollow. The knee supports can become טמא through מדרס, and they are allowed on שבת and in the עזרה. The chair and supports can become טמא through מדרס, but they are forbidden on שבת and in the עזרה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of סמוכות. In step 3 they are knee supports worn by someone who walks on his knees, and they are allowed. Here they belong with a chair used by someone who cannot walk at all, and they are forbidden.

phrases.english: His chair and supports are susceptible to treading-impurity,
phrases.notes: They are used for sitting and for pushing himself along.

phrases.english: and one may not go out with them on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: They are not treated as something worn, so this would be carrying.

phrases.english: and one may not enter the Temple courtyard with them.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the ruling for the knee supports.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a contrast with step 3. It keeps the same ruling on מדרס and reverses the rulings on שבת and the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crippled person's chair and supports can become טמא through מדרס, but they are forbidden on שבת and in the עזרה.

steps.title: לוקטמין are pure and may not be worn out on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's last ruling: לוקטמין cannot become טמא, and one may not go out with them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוקטמין are pure (they cannot become impure), and one may not go out with them on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final line of the משנה. It gives one more item and its two rulings: it is not subject to טומאה, and it may not be worn out on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא will explain later what לוקטמין are. They are 'pure' because they are not a real כלי, so they cannot receive טומאה. Even so, wearing them out on שבת is forbidden, because they are not ordinary clothing or a normal body support.

keyTerms.meaning: An item explained later in the גמרא (often understood as a kind of mask)
Pure; here it means they cannot become טמא at all
One may not go out wearing them on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: 'Pure' here does not mean 'permitted on שבת'. The טומאה question and the שבת question are separate, and in this case the answers go in opposite directions.

phrases.english: Lukatmin are pure,
phrases.notes: They are not a vessel, so they cannot become impure.

phrases.english: and one may not go out with them.
phrases.notes: This refers to going out on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the משנה's list of supports and devices, giving each one's טומאה status and שבת status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוקטמין are not susceptible to טומאה, and one may not go out with them on שבת.

steps.title: רבא asks how the dispute in the משנה should be read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבא asking רב נחמן which reading of the רבי מאיר / רבי יוסי dispute is correct. רב נחמן says he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא said to רב נחמן: How did we learn it? He said to him: I don't know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבא asks רב נחמן which תנא permits the קיטע to go out with his wooden leg and which one forbids it. רב נחמן admits he does not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different versions of the משנה apparently swapped the two names, so the reading itself was uncertain. This is a question about the wording of the text, not about the reasoning behind either side. 'I don't know' opens the door for other אמוראים to settle the text.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
How did we learn it? (What is the correct wording?)
I don't know

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rava said to Rav Nachman:
How did we learn it?
phrases.notes: Who permits and who forbids: רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי?

phrases.english: He said to him: I don't know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This opens the גמרא on the first dispute of the משנה, the קיטע case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct wording of the משנה: which תנא is lenient and which is strict.

steps.title: רבא asks what the practical law is
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the הלכה is. Again רב נחמן says he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the הלכה? He said to him: I don't know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries a second question: even without knowing the text, what is the practical ruling? רב נחמן again says he does not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה usually follows a known rule about which תנא we follow in a given dispute. But if you do not know which name goes with which opinion, you cannot apply that rule. The גמרא settles the reading in steps 8-12.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical law?

phrases.english: What is the halacha?
He said to him: I don't know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This follows up the question about the text with a question about the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical הלכה about a קיטע going out with his wooden leg.

steps.title: שמואל and רב הונא read the משנה as 'An amputee may not'
steps.stepSummary: An אמוראic tradition (איתמר) reports that both שמואל and רב הונא read the משנה as opening with 'אין הקיטע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: שמואל said: 'An amputee may not,' and likewise רב הונא said: 'An amputee may not.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a reported teaching that answers רבא's question about the text. שמואל and רב הונא both say the משנה reads 'אין הקיטע', meaning the amputee may not go out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the first opinion (רבי מאיר) forbids, and רבי יוסי is the one who permits. Two major אמוראים agree on this version, which gives it strong weight.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (a reported teaching of אמוראים)
The amputee may not (go out)
An amputee (someone missing a leg)

phrases.english: It was stated: Shmuel said:
'An amputee may not,'
phrases.notes: In this reading רבי מאיר forbids and רבי יוסי permits.

phrases.english: and likewise Rav Huna said: 'An amputee may not.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This supplies a reading of the text in answer to the unresolved question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה reads 'אין הקיטע': רבי מאיר forbids and רבי יוסי permits.

steps.title: רב יוסף adopts the reading of שמואל and רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that since both שמואל and רב הונא read 'אין הקיטע', we will also learn it that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Since שמואל said 'An amputee may not' and רב הונא said 'An amputee may not,' we too will learn 'An amputee may not.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף makes a decision about the text: we should follow the reading of these two authorities. This is the reading that will be challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's reasoning is simple: when two great authorities agree on a reading, we adopt it. Notice that this reading puts רבי יוסי on the lenient side. That will clash with the tradition from רב's study hall.

keyTerms.meaning: Since
We will learn/recite (the text this way)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Since Shmuel said 'An amputee may not'
and Rav Huna said 'An amputee may not' —
we too will learn 'An amputee may not.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This turns the reported readings into an adopted reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We adopt the reading 'אין הקיטע' (רבי מאיר forbids, רבי יוסי permits).

steps.title: רבא בר שירא objects by recalling a scene in רב's study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שירא challenges this: didn't they hear about the time רב חנן בר רבא taught the משנה to חייא בר רב in front of רב?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר שירא objected: Did they not hear what רב חנן בר רבא taught חייא בר רב before רב, in the small room of the study hall?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר שירא attacks רב יוסף's decision by pointing to an earlier tradition. This step sets up the scene, and the next step gives the actual content of what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is rhetorical. It means: you should have known about this incident, and it contradicts your reading. The tradition carries weight because רב himself was present and reacted. רב was שמואל's colleague and רב הונא's teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
Did they not hear?
A small room
The study hall

phrases.english: Rava bar Shira objected to it:
Did they not hear

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּמַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא
phrases.english: that which Rav Chanan bar Rava taught
to Chiyya bar Rav in front of Rav
in the small room of the study hall?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges רב יוסף's adopted reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's decision to read 'אין הקיטע' with רבי מאיר as the strict view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier tradition with רב present contradicts which names go with which opinions.

steps.title: רב signaled to reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: The reading recited was: 'The amputee may not go out with his wooden leg, says רבי מאיר, and רבי יוסי permits.' רב gestured: reverse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'An amputee may not go out with his wooden leg — the words of רבי מאיר; and רבי יוסי permits.' And רב signaled to him: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the content of רבא בר שירא's proof. When the reading named רבי מאיר as strict, רב signaled with his hand to switch the names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the switch, רבי מאיר permits and רבי יוסי forbids. That matches the version of our משנה in step 1. So the reading רב יוסף adopted, with רבי מאיר as the strict side, was the one רב corrected.

keyTerms.meaning: A wooden leg/foot
He signaled (with a gesture)
Reverse it

steps.confusionAlert: What רב reversed is which name goes with which opinion. The corrected version, which שמואל later quotes in step 14, reads 'הקיטע יוצא בקב שלו, דברי רבי מאיר; רבי יוסי אוסר'. After רב's correction, רבי יוסי is the one who forbids.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fixes the attributions used in step 1: רבי יוסי forbids the קב and רבי מאיר permits it.

phrases.english: An amputee may not go out with his wooden leg —
the words of Rabbi Meir;
and Rabbi Yosei permits.
And Rav signaled to him: Reverse it.
phrases.notes: After reversing, רבי מאיר permits and רבי יוסי forbids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the content of the incident cited in the objection.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי is the strict opinion and רבי מאיר the lenient one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's gesture correcting the recitation in his study hall.

steps.title: A memory aid: סמך-סמך
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory aid, 'סמך סמך': יוסי has a ס, and so does אוסר. So רבי יוסי is the one who forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: And the mnemonic is 'סמך, סמך.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this discussion with a memory trick that locks in רב's corrected reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ס appears in the name יוסי and in the word אוסר (forbids). Pairing them reminds you that רבי יוסי forbids the wooden leg. This confirms the version in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid (mnemonic)
The letter ס
Forbids

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: רבי מאיר permits the קיטע to go out with his wooden leg, and רבי יוסי forbids it. Remember it with 'סמך סמך': יוסי goes with אוסר.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
And the mnemonic is: 'samech, samech.'
phrases.notes: The ס in יוסי matches the ס in אוסר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives a mnemonic that cements the reversed reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי forbids and רבי מאיר permits the קיטע's wooden leg on שבת.

steps.title: שמואל also changed his mind, starting with the חליצה משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא claims that שמואל retracted his reading. It begins its proof by quoting a משנה that says חליצה done with a wooden sandal is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even שמואל changed his mind. As we learned in a משנה: if she did חליצה with a sandal that is not his, with a wooden sandal, or with a left sandal worn on the right foot, the חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that שמואל gave up his earlier reading of 'אין הקיטע'. It is setting up its proof by first quoting a משנה about חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail in this משנה is that a wooden sandal counts as a real shoe for חליצה. The next step will ask which תנא holds this. Whoever it is must hold that wooden footwear counts as a shoe, and that connects directly to the קיטע's wooden leg.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted / changed his mind
The ceremony that frees a childless widow from יבום, done by removing the brother-in-law's shoe
A wooden sandal
Valid

phrases.english: And even Shmuel retracted his view.
As we learned in a mishnah:
If she performed chalitza with a sandal that is not his,
with a wooden sandal,
or a left sandal on the right foot,
phrases.notes: The left-foot sandal worn on the right foot.

phrases.english: the chalitza is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that רבי יוסי forbids, the גמרא shows that שמואל himself came to agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל retracted his reading of 'אין הקיטע'. The supporting source is a משנה that validates חליצה with a wooden sandal.

steps.title: שמואל attributes the wooden sandal ruling to רבי מאיר using the reversed reading
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the חליצה משנה follows רבי מאיר, and he quotes the קיטע משנה in the form where רבי מאיר permits and רבי יוסי forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked: who is the תנא of that משנה? שמואל said: it is רבי מאיר. As we learned: the amputee may go out with his wooden leg, these are the words of רבי מאיר, and רבי יוסי forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof itself. When explaining the חליצה משנה, שמואל quotes the קיטע משנה in the reversed version, with רבי מאיר permitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only someone who treats wooden footwear as a real shoe could validate a wooden sandal for חליצה. שמואל names רבי מאיר as that person, because in his quote רבי מאיר permits the wooden leg. This shows that שמואל now accepts רב's reading, not his own earlier 'אין הקיטע' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the Tanna (whose view this is)?
The wooden stump or leg worn by an amputee
Forbids

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the order here: 'הקיטע יוצא' (the amputee may go out), with רבי מאיר permitting. This is the opposite of שמואל's original 'אין הקיטע' reading, and that is exactly the proof that he changed his mind.

phrases.english: And we said: Who is the tanna?
Shmuel said: It is Rabbi Meir,
as we learned in a mishnah:
The amputee may go out with his wooden leg,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir,
and Rabbi Yosei forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִינַן: מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that was set up in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל retracted and now holds that רבי מאיר permits the קב and רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's own identification of the תנא of the חליצה משנה, together with his quote of the קיטע משנה in the reversed form.

steps.title: רב הונא also changed his mind, starting with the plasterers' sandal ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא claims that רב הונא also retracted. It quotes a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא treats a plasterers' sandal as a real shoe, and the other חכמים did not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רב הונא changed his mind. As a ברייתא teaches: a plasterers' sandal can become impure with מדרס impurity, a woman may do חליצה with it, and one may go out in it on שבת. These are the words of רבי עקיבא, and they did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רב הונא. It sets up its proof by quoting a ברייתא about a plasterers' sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plasterers wore a cover over their shoes that was not a normal leather shoe. רבי עקיבא gives it the full status of a shoe for impurity, חליצה, and שבת. The ברייתא says the others disagreed, which sets up the next question about who exactly disagreed.

keyTerms.meaning: A plasterers' sandal: a cover worn over the shoes to protect them from lime
Can become impure when a זב treads or leans on it
And they did not agree with him

phrases.english: And even Rav Huna retracted his view,
as it was taught in a baraita:
A plasterers' sandal
is subject to midras impurity,
and a woman may perform chalitza with it,
and one may go out in it on Shabbat,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva,
and they did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 13: after שמואל, now רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא retracted his reading. The supporting source is a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא treats a plasterers' sandal as a shoe.

steps.title: A contradicting ברייתא says they did agree
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says the opposite: 'they agreed with him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: 'they agreed with him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two ברייתות contradict each other. One says the others disagreed with רבי עקיבא, and the other says they agreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions cannot be true about the same people. This contradiction sets up רב הונא's answer, and his answer will reveal how he reads the קיטע משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא)! (introduces a contradicting source)
They agreed with him

phrases.english: But it was taught: "They agreed with him"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ending 'ולא הודו לו' of the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'ולא הודו לו' in the plasterers' sandal ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel ברייתא records the opposite outcome ('הודו לו'), which is a direct contradiction.

steps.title: רב הונא: רבי מאיר agreed, רבי יוסי did not
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא resolves the contradiction by assigning 'agreed' to רבי מאיר and 'did not agree' to רבי יוסי. This shows that he too now holds that רבי יוסי forbids the wooden leg.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: who is the one who 'agreed with him'? רבי מאיר. And who is the one who 'did not agree with him'? רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers that each ברייתא is describing a different תנא. In doing so, he reveals that he now accepts the reversed reading of the קיטע משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agreeing with רבי עקיבא means treating a non-standard shoe as a real shoe, which fits someone who permits the wooden leg. רב הונא says that person is רבי מאיר, and that רבי יוסי is the one who disagrees. So רב הונא now holds that רבי מאיר permits and רבי יוסי forbids, which is exactly רב's reversed reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?

steps.whatToRemember: Both שמואל and רב הונא ended up agreeing with רב: in the קיטע משנה, רבי מאיר permits the wooden leg and רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whyThisMatters: Even the original supporters of 'אין הקיטע' changed their minds, so רב's reading (backed by 'סמך סמך') stands. In the next step רב יוסף offers a different way to resolve the contradiction between the ברייתות, one that does not involve רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Who is "they agreed with him"? Rabbi Meir,
and who is "they did not agree with him"? Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16, and in doing so proves the claim made in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different authorities: each ברייתא reflects a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to describe the same group of חכמים, so they appeared to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הודו לו' refers to רבי מאיר and 'לא הודו לו' refers to רבי יוסי. This fits רבי מאיר permitting and רבי יוסי forbidding the קב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא, like שמואל, accepted רב's reading: רבי יוסי forbids the wooden leg.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The one who disagreed was רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different answer to the contradiction between the ברייתות. The opinion 'they did not agree with him' belongs to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Who is the one behind 'they did not agree with him'? It is רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers his own way to settle the contradiction from Step 16. He does not use רב הונא's answer about רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says the חכמים agreed with רבי עקיבא, and the other says they did not. רב יוסף says most חכמים did agree, and the ברייתא that says 'they did not agree' is quoting one specific dissenter, רבי יוחנן בן נורי. In this answer, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי play no role at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not agree with him
A תנא who argues with רבי עקיבא

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Who is behind 'they did not agree with him'?
It is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאן ״לֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the contradiction, alongside רב הונא's answer in Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two ברייתות to different תנאים (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other about whether the חכמים agreed with רבי עקיבא
steps.terutzMaskana: Most חכמים agreed with him. The 'did not agree' ברייתא reflects רבי יוחנן בן נורי alone

steps.title: Proof: רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues with רבי עקיבא about straw items
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues with רבי עקיבא about simple straw and reed objects. This supports the idea that he would also argue about the plasterers' sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A container made of straw and a tube made of reeds — רבי עקיבא says they can become impure, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי says they cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף proves that רבי יוחנן בן נורי is known to argue with רבי עקיבא on exactly this kind of question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא counts simple, makeshift items as real כלים. רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not. So it fits that רבי יוחנן בן נורי would also refuse to count the makeshift plasterers' sandal as a real shoe.

keyTerms.meaning: A container (basket or hive) made of straw
A tube made of reeds
Rules that it can become impure
Rules that it cannot become impure

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
A container made of straw
and a tube made of reeds —
Rabbi Akiva says they can become impure,
and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says they cannot.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction between the ברייתות. רב הונא says it is רבי מאיר against רבי יוסי. רב יוסף says it is the חכמים against רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's answer in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן בן נורי is the one who 'did not agree' with רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a straw container and a reed tube

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: A plasterers' sandal is impure through treading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא: a plasterers' sandal can become טמא מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A plasterers' sandal can become impure through treading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can ask a question about it. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרס is a special kind of טומאה. It applies to an item made to carry a person's weight, such as something sat on, lain on, or walked on, when a זב puts his weight on it. The ruling here assumes this sandal counts as something made for walking.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said' — a formula for quoting an earlier source
A sandal worn by plasterers
Can become impure when a זב puts his weight on it

phrases.english: The Master said:
A plasterers' sandal
can become impure through treading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from Step 15 to examine one of its rulings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plasterers' sandal can become טמא מדרס

steps.title: Challenge: This sandal is not made for walking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the sandal can be טמא מדרס when it is not made for walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not made for walking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרס applies only to items made to support a person's weight in normal use. A plasterer wears this sandal while he works, not to walk around in. So it seems it should not be able to become טמא מדרס.

keyTerms.meaning: For walking
It is made

phrases.english: But it is not made for walking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a plasterers' sandal is טמא מדרס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מדרס needs an item made for walking or carrying weight, and a work sandal does not seem to be one

steps.title: Answer: The plasterer walks home in it
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב עולא answers that the plasterer does walk in the sandal on his way home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב עולא said: Because the plasterer walks in it until he reaches his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered: the sandal is used for walking after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though it is a work sandal, the plasterer usually walks home in it. That walking use is enough to make it count as a walking item, so it can become טמא מדרס.

keyTerms.meaning: A plasterer
Walks about

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עוּלָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Ulla said:
Because the plasterer walks in it
until he reaches his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עוּלָּא: שֶׁכֵּן הַסַּיָּיד מְטַיֵּיל בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts of how the item is used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sandal is used only for work, so it should not be טמא מדרס
steps.terutzMaskana: It is also used for walking home, so it can become טמא מדרס

steps.title: אביי: The wooden leg with a padding hollow gets only corpse impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a wooden leg with a hollow for padding. אביי says it can become טמא from a מת but not טמא מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if it has a receptacle for pads, it is impure.' אביי said: It can become impure through a corpse, but it cannot become impure through treading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's ruling about a wooden leg. אביי explains which kind of טומאה the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the hollow, the wooden leg counts as a container, so it can become טמא from a מת. But אביי holds that it cannot become טמא מדרס, because the person does not put his full weight on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A hollow space that can hold something
Pads or padding
Impurity that comes from a corpse

steps.confusionAlert: Here the argument is not about whether the wooden leg can become טמא at all. Both אביי and רבא agree it can. They only argue about which kind of טומאה it can receive.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית קִיבּוּל כְּתִיתִין —
phrases.english: And if it has a receptacle for pads —
it can become impure.
Abaye said:
It can become impure through a corpse,
but it cannot become impure through treading.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית קִיבּוּל כְּתִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining the משנה's ruling about the wooden leg
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wooden leg with a padding hollow can become טמא from a מת, but not טמא מדרס

steps.title: רבא: It can also become impure through treading
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי and says the wooden leg can also become טמא מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It can even become impure through treading.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that the wooden leg does support the person's weight enough to count for מדרס. So it can receive both kinds of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, also

phrases.english: Rava said:
It can even become impure through treading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's view in Step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wooden leg with a padding hollow can also become טמא מדרס

steps.title: רבא's proof: A child's walking wagon
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his view from a משנה that says a child's wagon is טמא מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say this? As we learned: A child's wagon can become impure through treading.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source to support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child's wagon helps the child walk, much like a wooden leg helps a person walk. The משנה says the wagon can become טמא מדרס, so רבא argues the wooden leg should be treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I derive this?
A small child's walking wagon

phrases.english: Rava said:
From where do I say this?
As we learned in a Mishnah:
A child's wagon —
can become impure through treading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's view in Step 24
steps.raayaObject: That a walking aid like the wooden leg can become טמא מדרס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that says a child's wagon is טמא מדרס

steps.title: אביי rejects the proof: The child leans on the wagon
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two cases are different. The child puts his weight on the wagon, but the person with the wooden leg does not put his full weight on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: There, he leans on it. Here, he does not lean on it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof and shows why it does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדרס depends on putting your full weight on an item. A child leans fully on his wagon. Someone with a wooden leg does not lean his full weight on it, so the comparison breaks down and אביי's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Leans his weight on it
There / here — a standard way of contrasting two cases

steps.whatToRemember: Whether an item can become טמא מדרס depends on whether a person truly puts his weight on it. אביי says this is why the wagon and the wooden leg are different.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
There, he leans on it;
here, he does not lean on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in Step 25
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רבא's position itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wagon carries the child's full weight, but the wooden leg does not carry the person's full weight

steps.title: אביי's proof from an old person's walking stick
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא that says an old person's walking stick is טהור from all types of טומאה. This supports his view that something a person does not fully lean on is not טמא מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know my view is right? Because a ברייתא teaches that an old person's walking stick is completely טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now gives a source to back up what he said about the wooden leg. He points to a ברייתא about an elderly person's walking stick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old person leans on a walking stick, but not with all of their weight. The ברייתא says the stick cannot become טמא at all. אביי reasons that the wooden leg is similar: a person does not put full weight on it, so it should not be טמא מדרס either.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (a speaker introducing a proof for his own view)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
A walking stick used by elderly people
Pure from everything, meaning it cannot become טמא in any way

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 25. There, רבא brought a proof for his side. Here, אביי is bringing a proof for his own side.

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught: A walking stick of the elderly
is pure from everything!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: In step 26, אביי pushed back against רבא's proof. Now he brings a positive proof for his own view.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that the wooden leg is not טמא מדרס, because a person does not lean on it with full weight
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: מַקֵּל שֶׁל זְקֵנִים טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם

steps.title: רבא begins to explain why the walking stick case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא would answer אביי's proof. It begins his reply with "הָתָם" ("there"), signaling that the walking stick case is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבא respond? He says: There, in the case of the walking stick...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to show how רבא pushes back on אביי's proof, and his full answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הָתָם points back to the walking stick case. It tells us רבא will argue that the stick is different from a wooden leg. If that is true, the ruling about the stick does not prove anything about the wooden leg.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבא? (a short way of asking how רבא answers this proof)
There, pointing back to the case the other side cited

phrases.english: And Rava? There, in the walking stick case,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is רבא's response to the proof אביי brought in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the walking stick, not the ברייתא's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The walking stick case is different from the wooden leg case, so it cannot be compared. The exact difference is explained on the next amud.
